title: Count Unguarded Cells in the Grid
summary: Given a grid of size m x n, along with the positions of guards and walls, determine the number of unoccupied cells that are not visible to any guard.
statement: Given a grid of size m x n, along with the positions of guards and walls, determine the number of unoccupied cells that are not visible to any guard. Guards can see in the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, and west) from their position, stopping if they encounter a wall or another guard. A cell is considered guarded if it can be seen by at least one guard.
constraints: Guards and walls occupy distinct grid cells.
A guard sees in four cardinal directions until a wall, guard, or boundary blocks the ray.
Count empty cells unseen by every guard.
hints: Store all occupied guard and wall coordinates as blockers.
Cast four rays from every guard, marking each empty cell until the first blocker or boundary.
Return total cells minus occupied cells minus the union of guarded cells.
Each ray matches one line of sight exactly, and the set counts cells seen by multiple guards only once.
editorial: Each ray matches one line of sight exactly, and the set counts cells seen by multiple guards only once.

tests.explanation: After all blocked sight lines are traced, seven empty cells remain unguarded.
The center guard sees its row and column, leaving the four corners unguarded.
